mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2% within a month indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% over three months signals a strong demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 2% over two months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to increased prices and reduced corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in 1 quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over a month, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.1%, signals a robust labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% over three months signals inflationary pressure, which can lead to monetary tightening and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent month-over-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the RSAFS shows consistent month-over-month increases.
